root_cause: The offcanvas element has data-bs-scroll="true" which sets the scroll configuration to true, preventing the focus trap from activating. Consequently, pressing Tab a second time moves focus outside the panel to the amount field.
repair_strategy: Remove the data-bs-scroll="true" attribute from the offcanvas element so that the scroll option defaults to false, allowing the focus trap to activate and keep focus inside the offcanvas when tabbing.

edits.before: <div class="offcanvas offcanvas-end" data-bs-scroll="true" data-bs-backdrop="true" tabindex="-1" id="help" aria-labelledby="help-title">\n
edits.after: <div class="offcanvas offcanvas-end" data-bs-backdrop="true" tabindex="-1" id="help" aria-labelledby="help-title">\n

expected_accessibility_effect: Focus remains trapped inside the offcanvas panel when tabbing; the second Tab press keeps focus on the #help-close button (or cycles to the first focusable element) instead of moving to the amount field outside the panel.
functional_risks: Removing data-bs-scroll="true" may change scrolling behavior when the offcanvas is open; however, the offcanvas is narrow and unlikely to require body scrolling, so the impact is minimal.
verification_requirements: After opening the help panel with Enter, pressing Tab once should focus the #help-close button.
Pressing Tab a second time should keep focus inside the panel (either on #help-close or loop to the first focusable element).
Verify that the offcanvas content can still be scrolled internally if needed.
